I've been working this land for 40 years. My father farmed it before me. I don't need books to tell me what to do — I know this soil, I know Quzhou's weather, I know what works.

My 6 mu runs wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as always. The wheat and maize share the same ground — they just take turns.

**For wheat:** I'll plant in mid-October once the soil cools down. I'll buy improved seed from the county supply store — the local variety everyone around here uses. I know how it grows. Before planting I'll do a rotary pass and put down diammonium phosphate and some urea as base fertilizer. Then I'll topdress urea again at jointing. Four irrigations: once at planting to get germination, once in December before the ground freezes, once at jointing in April, once at heading in May. I'll spray herbicide in early spring and check for powdery mildew and aphids before harvest. Two of us can handle this.

**For maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June, I'll direct-seed hybrid maize into the stubble. No need to till again — saves time on a hot June day, and the ground is fine. Hybrid seed is the only thing worth planting for maize now. I'll put fertilizer down at planting and topdress at tasseling. Summer rains usually help — I'll irrigate at planting and once more at grain fill if it looks dry. One herbicide spray right after emergence. Most years that's enough.

Two people, 6 mu — we manage fine.
